Definition: to be wise (in mind, word or act)
BiblicalUsage: Chakam is the verb, to be wise, and it is used for scheming as well as for sense. Pharaoh said, let us deal wisely with the Hebrews, lest they multiply; Moses wished Israel were wise enough to consider their latter end; Solomon was wiser than all men; and Elihu says great men are not always wise.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe this word warns me that wisdom can be a weapon: Pharaoh's wisdom was cruelty with a plan, and Solomon's was a gift with a name. The difference is whether wisdom bows to God or uses Him.
